core_obligations: Decency: quasi-separatedness makes the stack decent (proof lines 10694-10695)
Quasi-compact inertia: quasi-separatedness makes the diagonal quasi-compact, and the inertia morphism is the base change of the diagonal by itself, hence quasi-compact (proof lines 10696-10699)

Conclusion: reducedness, decency, irreducibility of the space and quasi-compactness of the inertia are exactly the hypotheses in the definition of an integral stack, so the stack is integral; the proof also notes that quasi-separatedness may be replaced by quasi-compactness of the diagonal (proof lines 10700-10704)
proof_roadmap: 准分离 ⇒ Δ 准紧；惯性 I_X → X 是 Δ 沿 Δ 的基变换 ⇒ I_X → X 准紧。
把「既约 + decent + 惯性质紧（+ 空间不可约）」逐条对上整性的定义即得；并指出准分离可换成 Δ_X 准紧。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that an algebraic stack which is reduced and quasi-separated with irreducible underlying space is integral (author lemma at source lines 10686-10691, label lemma-totaro-case). The proof (source lines 10693-10705) derives decency from quasi-separatedness, obtains quasi-compactness of the inertia from quasi-compactness of the diagonal by base change, and checks the clauses of the definition of an integral stack while recording the sharper hypothesis (proof lines 10694-10704). The verification of the defining clauses through the diagonal and the inertia is the content. H3.
